title: fix(objectql)!: a user field's declared deleteBehavior takes effect when the user is deleted (#29253)
body:
domain:server#5 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmQKwKFCp1m6Pb6Q8c1

<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9C3uenhvETo3EhaCvXV7GjQ)_

Fixes #29253

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: semantic
Skills-docs: follow-up #29400 — skills/objectstack-data/rules/field-types.md (the `user` row lists no `deleteBehavior`), skills/objectstack-data/rules/relationships.md; `content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx` is updated here

**BREAKING** for an app that declares `deleteBehavior` on a `user` field: the declared value now takes effect when the user is deleted. A delete of a user held by a `restrict` field (or a `required` field declaring `set_null`) is now refused with `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED` where it succeeded; a declared `cascade` now deletes the holding rows; a declared `set_null` now clears them. **The fix:** if you declared `deleteBehavior` on a `user` field only as documentation, remove it or change it to what you want enforced.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：user 字段上作者写明的 deleteBehavior 现在真的生效——删除用户时，restrict 拒绝删除（409 DELETE_RESTRICTED），cascade 删掉持有该用户的记录，set_null 清空该字段（多值字段只移除该成员）；没写 deleteBehavior 的 user 字段行为不变。
- 为什么改：spec 接受并保留 user 字段上的 deleteBehavior，但引擎的删除联动只认 master_detail / lookup / tree，user 字段上的声明一直是摆设，被删用户的 id 残留在记录里。
- 风险与回滚：席位裁定为收紧（narrowing，BREAKING，objectql minor）：写了 restrict（或 required + set_null）的应用，删除被引用的用户从 200 变成 409；写了 cascade 的会连带删记录。#9784 之前存下的对象可能在 user 字段上带着自动写入的 set_null，现在也会生效。仓内平台对象和示例里没有这样的字段。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：packages/objectql/src/engine.ts（statesDeleteSemantics 与 deleteWalkTargetOf），packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-delete-user-field.test.ts，packages/objectql/src/federated-injected-column-readers.test.ts（台账两行）。
- 两分钟验证：pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run src/engine-cascade-delete-user-field.test.ts，预期 16 条全绿。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

**Measured first: which doors delete a user** (at `origin/main` `b1779200`):

| Door | Reaches `ObjectQL.delete` (so the walk runs)? | Code path |
|---|---|---|
| better-auth admin remove-user, self delete-user (and its callback) | yes, by id, as the system | `internalAdapter.deleteUser` deletes the `user` model through the plugin-auth adapter: `objectql-adapter.ts` `delete` / `deleteMany` call `dataEngine.delete(objectName, { where: { id } })`, and `dataEngine.delete` is `e.delete(m, asAttributedSystem(q))` (`isSystem: true`). The request runs inside `runSubjectErasureAtomically` (`SESSION_ERASURE_PATHS`), so a refusal rolls the credential rows back. |
| Generic data doors (REST `DELETE /data/sys_user/:id`, MCP / batch data tools) | refused before the delete | `identity-write-guard.ts` registers a `beforeDelete` that refuses a caller-context write to any `managedBy: 'better-auth'` object (ADR-0092 D2); `sys_user` declares no generic delete (`userActions: { edit: true }` only). |
| Ban / soft delete | not a delete | `admin-ban-endpoints.ts` updates the user and deletes its sessions; the `sys_user` row stays. |

Every door that removes the `sys_user` row reaches the walk, so this is (B) enforce, and no spec change.

**The change** (`packages/objectql/src/engine.ts` only):

- `statesDeleteSemantics` (the one family test every reader of the walk asks) admits a `user` field when, and only when, it declares a `deleteBehavior` of the enum's three values. A `user` field that declares none stays out: the spec's parse materializes no value on it, and the engine invents no default.
- `deleteWalkTargetOf` (new) answers the object a relation points at for `cascadeRelationBehavior` and `planCascadeAtomicity`. It still reads the `reference` carrier through `referenceCarrierOf`, so an unreadable carrier still throws; for a `user` field it answers `referenceTargetOf` (`sys_user`), so a `{ type: 'user' }` with no `reference` still points at the user.
- Nothing else moves: an admitted `user` field then goes through the walk exactly as a `lookup` with the same authored value, including the multi-value `$contains` probe and member removal, the required `set_null` → `restrict` escalation, the two-phase cascade set and the one-transaction plan.

`DELETE_SEMANTICS_REFERENCE_TYPES` keeps `master_detail`, `lookup`, `tree`; its docblock's old "`user` stays out … made in the spec, never here" paragraph is replaced by the declared-only rule above.

Docs: one paragraph in `content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx` (Referential integrity). Changeset: `.changeset/29253-user-field-delete-behavior.md`, `@objectstack/objectql` **minor** (the level a semantic metadata-protocol kind takes), with the BREAKING banner, the one-line fix, and the ADR-0087 disposition `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: no schema key, export or type moves, and there is no stored value for a conversion to rewrite.

## Tests

New `packages/objectql/src/engine-cascade-delete-user-field.test.ts` (16 tests; the real `ObjectQL` over a stub driver with snapshot rollback, whose WHERE matcher answers `$or` / `$and` / `$in` / `$contains` and throws on any other operator). Deletes go through the engine with and without the adapter's system context:

- no `deleteBehavior` (parsed single, parsed multi, raw, required): the user is deleted and the holder keeps the id;
- `restrict`, single and multi-valued: `DELETE_RESTRICTED` / 409 naming the holder's object, both rows kept; the same code and status a `lookup` restrict to `sys_user` answers; a user nobody holds still deletes; a `user` field with no `reference` still refuses;
- `cascade`, single and multi-valued: the holders are deleted, a row holding another user stays; a later `restrict` rolls the cascade back;
- `set_null`: single cleared to `null`; multi loses only the member, an emptied set is `[]`; required `set_null` refuses.

**Forced test edit:** `packages/objectql/src/federated-injected-column-readers.test.ts` (the #21918 reader ledger). The two `referenceCarrierOf()` seam uses moved from `cascadeRelationBehavior` / `planCascadeAtomicity` into `deleteWalkTargetOf`, so the two old `skips` rows are replaced by two `not-a-read` rows for the helper. The two callers' own `isFederatedUnprovisionedInjectedColumn()` rows stay and still bind the skip.

## Acceptance notes

- Behaviour that changes for an app: a `user` field that declares `restrict`, or `set_null` with `required: true`, now refuses deleting the user it holds (409, was 200); `cascade` now deletes the holders; `set_null` now clears them. A repo-wide scan of `Field.user(` / `type: 'user'` declarations under `packages/` and `examples/` found none that declares `deleteBehavior`.
- Rows stored before #9784: the spec's parse then wrote `deleteBehavior: 'set_null'` on every field type, `user` included, so an object stored in that era can carry a `set_null` on a `user` field no author wrote. It now takes effect (cleared on user delete; refused on a `required` field). Stated in the changeset; the seat accepted it with no spec card.
- The two declaration lines above were ruled by seat 5 after round 1 (a narrowing, semantic kind); the dispatch claim carried no arm and kind none.
- Spec prose left as it is (no `packages/spec/**` edit on this card): the `FieldSchema` `.overwrite` comment in `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts` still says a `user` field sits outside the walk's family; true for a bare one, no longer for an authored one.
- `os verify --delete-behaviors` reports an authored `user` field `not-derivable` (its target `sys_user` is not an app-declared object), so that family does not start probing these fields.

## Verification

`return false; // ABLATION-29253` in place of the `user` arm of `statesDeleteSemantics` (the walk on `main`): `Tests 10 failed | 6 passed (16)`. Every restrict / cascade / set_null pin fails (five with "expected the delete to be refused"); the four no-`deleteBehavior` controls stay green.
</details>

1. `user` arm answers `false` (user out of the walk, as on `main`): `Tests 10 failed | 6 passed (16)`.
2. `deleteWalkTargetOf` answers the carrier only: `Tests 1 failed | 15 passed (16)`, only "a user field naming no reference still references sys_user".
3. `user` arm answers `true` (every user field joins, a bare one defaulting to `set_null`): `Tests 4 failed | 12 passed (16)`, the four no-`deleteBehavior` controls (e.g. `expected { person: null } to match { person: 'r_1' }`, multi `expected { person: [] }`).
</details>
